question: Should the V60 SNDK pressure-short route add a fixed target or completed-bar trailing profit lock?

historical_input.coverage: approximately 22.2 million archived L2 rows from February through August, aggregated into causal 15-minute midpoint bars
historical_input.limitation: The replay is not exact live fresh-15-second decision and one-minute venue-mark lifecycle parity.

bounded_candidates.selection_result: No candidate passed nonnegative stress net, nonnegative worst-fold net, and positive net excluding the largest winner on development.

live_ledger_contradictory_evidence.scope: current exact SNDK short-only provider execution identity
live_ledger_contradictory_evidence.interpretation: This is favorable but single-trade evidence. It contradicts treating winner concentration as sufficient reason to disable a positive-skew breakout route, but it does not establish route expectancy or validate the time fallback.

method_deviation.description: Fixed-target validation arms were inspected during diagnostics even though no fixed target passed development selection.
method_deviation.effect: Those validation values were excluded from promotion. No candidate was promoted, so the final decision remains based on development rejection and preservation of the control contract. A null metric means it was not retained in the diagnostic record and is not inferred here.

successor.normalized_change: profile identity only; every V60 execution, sizing, route, and runtime contract is preserved

risks: The historical development sample is negative under every evaluated exit, so current-route expectancy remains uncertain.
The only exact current-identity live close is a winner and cannot estimate variance, loss rate, or cadence.
A no-target trend exit can give back open profit before the stop or time fallback; the tested alternatives reduced aggregate replay results but do not exhaust all causal exit designs.
The historical midpoint-bar proxy can disagree with exact live marks, book liquidity, latency, and signal timing.
falsifiers_and_update_triggers: Two or more additional exact-identity SNDK closes produce negative net expectancy after fees and funding.
A prospectively frozen exact-route exit challenger beats the control after costs across independent windows without largest-winner dependence.
Live protection, maximum-hold enforcement, ledger attribution, or provider-side authority fails reconciliation.
Exact fresh-15-second lifecycle replay reverses the midpoint-proxy conclusion.
